newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December S&P 500s finish near all-time highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December S&P 500s finish near all-time highs.

text.p: The U.S. December Standard & Poor's 500 contract finished near its all-time high as a strong rally in U.S. bonds pushed rates to lows last seen in April, traders and analysts said.
Dealers continued to buy S&P futures late in the day, pushing December closer to its contract high of 718.70, after the U.S. bond futures market closed at 1400 CST/2000 GMT.
December bonds set an eight-month high of 114-02/32, as the yield on the 30-year T-bond edged below 6.60 percent and increased the attractiveness of the stock market's rate of return, they said.
December S&Ps were on the verge of retesting 718.70 in late afternoon trade, but only mustered gains to 718.35.
"That is exactly the sort of thing that will keep people bearish in the near term," said Michael de la Maza, president of Redfire Capital Management.
He said that bearish sentiment, which was reflected by the "enormous" amount of put-to-call buying in the S&P 100 market on Tuesday, would prove to be a contrary indicator.
"A two percent rally is in the works from here to the end of next week," de la Maza said about his forecasts for December to rise to 730.00 by the end of next week.
"This will segue into a December-type bullishness," he said, adding that he is looking for December S&Ps to end the year around the 740.00 area.
Fair value was about 2.40 points, using a blended rate, while arbitrage buy programs were roughly 3.20 points over cash S&Ps. Arbitrage sell programs were at 2.10 points.
Traders and analysts said expectations that the Republicans would maintain control of Congress contributed to the rally in both U.S. bonds and stocks.

At settlement, December S&P 500s were up 4.15 points at 715.40, Russell 2000s gained 0.95 point to 342.25, Value Line futures were off 0.10 point to 648.00, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 25.0 to 20680.0 and Midcap 400s advanced 0.45 point to 245.40. --Chicago Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750
